newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate steady, long-term bills climb.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate steady, long-term bills climb.

text.p: * Tax remittances, 10-year bond auction keep market edgy

Philippine call money was unchanged at 10.53125 percent, but long-term Treasury bill rates were slightly higher as banks sold their holdings in anticipation of possible liquidity tightness next week, traders said.
Traders were expecting a huge fund outflow on Monday due to the quarterly value added tax payment which was estimated to range between 10 and 15 billion pesos.
The ten-year bond auction on Tuesday would also siphon off five billion pesos from the system, a trader said.
"Right now, banks are cautious on their positions because of the two events. No one is really sure whether the present liquidity level will dry up or not," he added.

Some banks were cashing in their long-term bills in preparation of the possible liquidity crunch. "There are some aggressive sellers in the market, driving the secondary rates higher," another trader said.
The expectation of a rebound in the T-bill auction rates on Monday also compounded the profit-taking.
Three-month bills were being bid between 10.7 and 10.85 percent, and offered between 10.60 and 10.675 percent.
Six-month bills were being bid between 11.075 and 11.25 percent, and offered between 10.90 and 11.05 percent.
One-month bills were being bid between 11.45 and 11.625 percent and sold between 11.35 and 11.415 percent.
The overnight money was stuck at 10.53125 percent for the 14th consecutive session. A meagre 2.7 billion pesos changed hands in the interbank call loan market.
